issues.legal_issue: A sole eyewitness’s testimony may be accepted as reliable despite challenges to the witness’s presence, conduct, and relationship to the victims when the account is natural and consistent with the circumstances.
material_facts: The sole eyewitness was related to one of the victims and testified that he saw the accused at the scene during the killings.
His presence was explained by a family dispute over land and a planned meeting about that dispute the following day.
He testified that he fled to protect himself after seeing armed men and hearing gunfire.
His account was simple and consistent, including his statement that the principal accused was unarmed.
issues.conclusion: The eyewitness’s testimony was natural, trustworthy, and reliable; the challenges to it were rejected.
issues.legal_principle: There are no hard-and-fast rules for assessing witness veracity. The witness’s simplicity, consistency, and conduct must be considered in the circumstances of the case; human behaviour varies with the circumstances, and a witness’s relationship to a victim does not by itself make the testimony unreliable. No earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and sole_witness_account_consistent and witness_presence_explained and witness_conduct_reasonable

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.sole_witness_account_consistent: The sole eyewitness gave a consistent account of the events.
predicates.witness_presence_explained: The circumstances of the case explain why the eyewitness was present at the scene.
predicates.witness_conduct_reasonable: The eyewitness’s conduct before, during, or after the event is understandable in the circumstances.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction appeal involves a consistent sole eyewitness whose presence and conduct are explained, the testimony is accepted as reliable.

issues.legal_issue: Medical and forensic evidence that corroborates an eyewitness account can sustain a conviction despite claims that the manner of the injuries made the prosecution account impossible or that physical evidence was planted.
material_facts: The victims had gunshot injuries, and the evidence did not establish a fixed time within which the killings had to have occurred.
The victims were killed inside rooms, and no witness saw the killings inside those rooms.
Cartridges were recorded at the scene in an early inquest report, before the later seizure of the weapons.
Forensic examination matched recovered cartridges to firearms associated with the accused, and other recovered items were found to correspond with items linked to the accused.
The accused who asserted an alibi did not call witnesses to support it.
issues.conclusion: The challenges to the medical and forensic evidence were rejected; the eyewitness account and corroborating evidence established guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
issues.legal_principle: The court assessed the evidence as a whole. The medical evidence did not establish that the killings had to occur within a time incompatible with the firearms relied on by the prosecution, and the contemporaneous record of cartridges at the scene contradicted the claim that they were planted later. The court relied on the criminal standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt; no earlier case was relied on for this issue.

rule.if: criminal_conviction_appeal and gunshot_injuries_established and forensic_matches_linked_ammunition_to_weapons and early_scene_recorded_ammunition and corroborating_evidence_supported_eye_witness

predicates.criminal_conviction_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.gunshot_injuries_established: Medical evidence established that the victims sustained gunshot injuries.
predicates.forensic_matches_linked_ammunition_to_we: Forensic examination linked recovered ammunition to firearms associated with the accused.
predicates.early_scene_recorded_ammunition: A record made at the scene before the later weapon seizures noted ammunition there.
predicates.corroborating_evidence_supported_eye_wit: Other evidence supported material parts of the eyewitness’s account.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction appeal includes established gunshot injuries, forensic and early scene evidence linking ammunition to weapons, and other evidence supporting the eyewitness, the conviction is supported beyond reasonable doubt.

issues.legal_issue: A brutal multiple killing does not warrant the death penalty as a rarest-of-rare case when there is no evidence of prior misconduct or a continuing threat to society and the offenders may be reformed or rehabilitated.
material_facts: The appeal challenged death sentences imposed for the killing of eight members of two families in a brutal crime motivated by a land dispute.
There was no evidence of prior misconduct by the accused.
There was no evidence that the accused posed a continuing threat to society or could not be reformed or rehabilitated.
issues.conclusion: The death sentences were set aside and replaced with imprisonment for life.
issues.legal_principle: The court applied the rarest-of-rare standard and considered the possibility of reform or rehabilitation and whether the offenders posed a continuing threat to society. It relied on Prakash Dhawal Khairnar (Patil) v. State of Maharashtra, (2002) 2 SCC 35, and Ram Anup Singh v. State of Bihar, JT 2002 (5) 621, which treated heinous killings arising from a land dispute as insufficient for the death penalty where a continuing societal threat and inability to reform were not established.

rule.if: criminal_appeal_from_death_sentence and brutal_multiple_killings and no_prior_misconduct_evidence and no_evidence_of_continued_social_threat and reform_or_rehabilitation_not_ruled_out

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_death_sentence: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging a death sentence.
predicates.brutal_multiple_killings: The crime involved the brutal killing of multiple victims.
predicates.no_prior_misconduct_evidence: The record contains no evidence of the offenders’ prior misconduct.
predicates.no_evidence_of_continued_social_threat: The record contains no evidence that the offenders would pose a continuing threat to society.
predicates.reform_or_rehabilitation_not_ruled_out: The record does not establish that the offenders cannot be reformed or rehabilitated.

issues.definition: When an appeal from a death sentence concerns brutal multiple killings but the record shows no prior misconduct or continuing social threat and does not rule out reform, the death sentence is replaced with life imprisonment.
